items.label: text
items.text: If there isn't enough air (or oxygen), you get incomplete combustion. This leads to the formation of carbon (soot) or carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide.

items.label: text
items.text: For example, if methane burns in a badly maintained gas appliance, there may not be enough oxygen available to produce carbon dioxide, and so you get toxic carbon monoxide instead:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 C H _ { 4 } ( g ) + 3 O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 C O ( g ) + 4 H _ { 2 } O ( 1 )

items.label: text
items.text: The formation of carbon monoxide from the incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons is very dangerous. Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless, and is very poisonous. Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it reduces the ability of the blood to carry oxygen around the body. This will make you ill, or you may even die, because not enough oxygen gets to the cells in your body for respiration to provide energy.

items.label: section_header
items.text: DID YOU KNOW?

items.label: text
items.text: Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin (the molecule that carries oxygen in the red blood cells), preventing it from carrying the oxygen. It binds more strongly to the haemoglobin than oxygen does.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTENSIONWORK

items.label: text
items.text: If you try to draw a dot-and-cross diagram for carbon monoxide, you will see that it is a very strange molecule because carbon does not form four bonds.

items.label: text
items.text: Refinery gases are a mixture of methane, ethane, propane and butane, which can be separated into individual gases if required. These gases are commonly used as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for domestic heating and cooking.

items.label: text
items.text: As with all the other fractions, petrol is a mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points. It is used as a fuel in cars.

items.label: text
items.text: Kerosene is used as a fuel for jet aircraft, as domestic heating oil and as 'paraffin' for small heaters and lamps.
